notes.no_data: Use a number you researched yourself. Vukoli has no salary data. Mike's budget is built from these numbers.
notes.practice: Practice settings, not real recruiter data.
notes.tough_practice: Practice only. Not a prediction of a hiring decision.
notes.personal: In many places this may not be a lawful question. Rules differ by country, so check the rules where the job is.

styles.name: Friendly
styles.blurb: Warm and open to a fair ask. Moves when you give a reason.

styles.name: Firm
styles.blurb: Polite but steady. Needs a reason, and stops moving if you repeat yourself.

styles.name: Tight budget
styles.blurb: Starts low, moves little, and pushes for a quick yes.

styles.name: Surprise me
styles.blurb: Mike picks a style at random. You see which in the debrief.

cards.title: Know your number, then pick who goes first
cards.rule: If you know your number, say it first, a little above your target and precise (97,250, not 100,000). If you do not, ask for their range.
cards.evidence: Lab studies on anchors and precise numbers. Who should go first is debated for job offers.
cards.example: Based on the scope, I'm looking at 96,500.

cards.title: Ask for their range
cards.rule: Asking first is a fair move, not a dodge.
cards.example: Before I give a number, what range did you plan for this role?

cards.title: Keep your current pay private
cards.rule: Talk about what the role is worth. In some places employers may not be allowed to ask.
cards.evidence: Law in some places, plus common advice
cards.example: I'd rather focus on what this role is worth. What range did you plan for it?

cards.title: Pause before you answer
cards.rule: Two or three seconds help you think. It is not a pressure trick.
cards.example: Thank you. Let me think about that for a second.

cards.title: Give a reason with every number
cards.rule: Tie the ask to results or scope, not to your costs. Keep it warm.
cards.example: I've led two launches like this one, so I'm asking for 98,000.

cards.title: If base is stuck, ask about the package
cards.rule: Sign-on, an earlier review, days off, remote days, title.
cards.evidence: Studies on multi-issue offers, plus common advice
cards.example: If base is fixed, could we add a sign-on bonus or a review at six months?

cards.title: Only mention offers you really have
cards.rule: Name the timing, not the amount. Bluffs get checked.
cards.evidence: Studies on alternatives, plus common advice
cards.example: I have another offer and need to answer by Friday.

cards.title: Ask for time and the terms in writing
cards.rule: A few days is a normal request.
cards.evidence: Common advice, one study on short deadlines
cards.example: Could you send the full terms? I'll reply by Thursday.

cards.title: Bridge the gap with a step-up
cards.rule: If they cannot reach your number now, agree on it later: the offer now, your number after the probation or in six months.
cards.example: If 90,000 is the limit today, could we agree on 98,000 after the three-month probation?

cards.title: Make the step-up real
cards.rule: Amount, date, what you need to show, and in the offer letter. A promise said aloud is not a deal.
cards.example: Great. Can we write the 98,000 at three months and the goals into the offer?

cards.title: Personal question: acknowledge, fact, redirect
cards.rule: Stay calm and short, then go back to the job.
cards.example: My plans won't affect my work. Can I tell you about my availability?

cards.title: Pushed back: say "fair point", then go shorter
cards.rule: Restate the core of your answer with one result.
cards.example: Fair point. In short: I cut release time by a third.

questions.text: What kind of salary do you have in mind?
questions.follow_up: I need an actual figure, not a range.
questions.checking: Whether your number fits their budget, and how you value yourself.
questions.trap: Naming a low number, or refusing flatly.
questions.shape: Give the context, ask for their range, and if pressed give a number tied to the role. Say you are flexible on the whole package.

questions.text: And what do they pay you right now?
questions.follow_up: It's a simple question. Why not tell me?
questions.trap: Telling them, or making a number up.
questions.shape: Decline kindly, move to what this role is worth, and ask for their range.

questions.text: Our budget is lower than you'd hoped. Still interested?
questions.follow_up: So what would make it work for you?
questions.checking: How you react to a number.
questions.trap: An instant yes, or visible disappointment.
questions.shape: Pause, thank them, ask what the package includes, and say what would make it work.

questions.text: If I made you an offer right now, would you say yes today?
questions.follow_up: Most people just say yes. Why wait?
questions.checking: Whether you can be pushed to close.
questions.trap: Saying yes only to show enthusiasm.
questions.shape: Show interest, then ask for the offer in writing and a little time.

questions.text: We can't match what you earn now. Is that a deal-breaker?
questions.follow_up: Be honest, how big a step down can you take?
questions.shape: Acknowledge it, talk about the value of the whole role, and offer to look for a package that works.

questions.text: Why do you want to leave your current job?
questions.follow_up: That sounds like you don't get along with them.
questions.checking: Your attitude and how stable you are.
questions.shape: One neutral reason, the pull toward this role, and one line about what you learned.

questions.text: Were you laid off?
questions.follow_up: Why you and not someone else?
questions.checking: Whether you are honest about it.
questions.trap: A defensive or very long story.
questions.shape: State the fact plainly, say how big the event was (team or company), and say what you did next.

questions.text: There's half a year missing on your CV. What happened?
questions.follow_up: So you weren't working at all?
questions.checking: Your explanation and whether you are ready now.
questions.shape: A short reason, what you did in that time (learning, projects), and why you are ready now.

questions.text: Who else are you interviewing with?
questions.follow_up: Any offers on the table yet?
questions.checking: How much competition there is, and how urgent it is.
questions.shape: Answer truthfully and in general terms. Say your interest in this role is high.

questions.text: What's your biggest weakness?
questions.follow_up: Everyone says that one. Give me a real one.
questions.trap: A fake weakness such as working too hard.
questions.shape: A real weakness that is not core to the job, one thing you do about it, and a sign of progress.

questions.text: What would your manager say you need to fix?
questions.follow_up: When did they last tell you that?
questions.shape: One specific point from real feedback, and what you did about it.

questions.text: Tell me about a project that failed.
questions.follow_up: Whose fault was it?
questions.shape: The context, your decision, the impact, the lesson, and how it changed your later work.

questions.text: When were you wrong in front of your team?
questions.follow_up: What did you change afterwards?
questions.shape: The fact, your share of it, and what you changed.

questions.text: Honestly, you look overqualified for this.
questions.follow_up: Won't you be bored in six months?
questions.checking: Whether you will stay and be happy.
questions.shape: Say what you want from this role, how it fits your plan, and how you will use the extra experience.

questions.text: You don't have the experience we listed.
questions.follow_up: Why should we take that risk?
questions.checking: Honesty and how fast you learn.
questions.shape: Admit the gap, give the nearest evidence, and offer a concrete 30-day plan.

questions.text: Why us and not one of our competitors?
questions.follow_up: That's on our website. What else?
questions.shape: Two specifics about their product or team, and one honest difference.

questions.text: Why switch careers now?
questions.follow_up: Isn't this just running away from the old job?
questions.checking: Your reason and the risk you carry.
questions.shape: The pull toward the new field, what you already bring, and proof that you committed (a project, a course).

questions.text: Why you over someone with more years?
questions.follow_up: That doesn't convince me yet.
questions.shape: Two strengths tied to this role, evidence for each, and how fast you learn.

questions.text: Is your English strong enough for this team?
questions.follow_up: What happens when you don't understand someone in a meeting?
questions.trap: Apologising too much, or denying any difficulty.
questions.shape: A calm fact, evidence that you work in English, and how you handle an unclear moment.

questions.text: Will you need a visa from us?
questions.follow_up: How long would that take?
questions.shape: A direct answer, your current status, and a rough timeline.

questions.text: Can you say that again in simpler words?
questions.shape: Say it again in two short sentences.

questions.text: How old are you, if you don't mind?
questions.checking: Energy, cost and risk, often through bias.
questions.shape: Acknowledge, stay calm, and go back to your experience and what you would bring.

questions.text: Are you planning to have kids soon?
questions.trap: Telling them, or answering with hostility.
questions.shape: Say your plans will not affect your commitment, then offer facts about your availability.

questions.text: Any health issues we should know about?
questions.shape: Say you can do the essential duties and ask if something specific about the role worries them.

questions.text: Are you allowed to work here without sponsorship?
questions.checking: Your right to work. This form of the question is usually lawful.
questions.trap: Mixing it up with the unlawful questions.
questions.shape: Answer directly: you are authorised to work here, or you will need sponsorship.

tough_lines.opening: {hi} I'm Mike. This is a round of tough questions, {count} of them. Some are uncomfortable on purpose. Take your time. {question}
tough_lines.closing: Okay. That was my last question. Thank you. You can end the session now to see your debrief.
tough_lines.move_on: Okay, thank you. Let's move on.

pressure.long: Okay, stop. Give me the short version.
pressure.no_result: And what actually came of it?
pressure.apology: You don't need to apologise. Just answer.
pressure.rehearsed: That sounds rehearsed. Try once more.

opening.friendly: {hi} I'm Mike, from the recruiting team. We'd love to move forward on the {role} role. Before I share details, what are you expecting for the salary?
opening.firm: {hi} I'm Mike, from recruiting. We're ready to talk about the {role} role. What salary are you expecting?
opening.tight: {hi} I'm Mike, from recruiting. I have a short window today for the {role} role. What salary are you looking for?

press_number.friendly: I'd like a number to work with. What are you looking for?
press_number.firm: I need a number to move on. What are you looking for?
press_number.tight: I need a number to move on. What are you looking for?

ask_figure.*: Sorry, I didn't catch a figure. What number would work for you?

state_offer.friendly: Thanks for sharing. Here is where we are: we can offer {amount} base per year. How does that sound?
state_offer.firm: Here is what I can offer: {amount} base per year. What do you think?
state_offer.tight: Our offer is {amount} base per year. That's standard for the role. What do you think?

confirm_number.*: That fits what we planned. We can offer {amount} base per year. Shall we go ahead?

concede.friendly: That's a fair point. I can move to {amount} base per year.
concede.firm: Okay, I can stretch to {amount} base per year.
concede.tight: I can move a little, to {amount} base per year.

concede_final.friendly: That's a fair point. I can move to {amount} base per year, and that's the best I can do on base.
concede_final.firm: I can stretch to {amount} base per year. That is as far as base goes.
concede_final.tight: I can move to {amount} base per year. That is final on base.

over_budget.friendly: I hear you, but that's above what we can do on base. I can offer {amount} base per year.
over_budget.firm: That's above what we can do on base. My offer is {amount} base per year.
over_budget.tight: That's above what we can do on base. The offer stays at {amount} base per year.

hold_confirm.*: Happy to confirm {amount} base per year. Shall we go ahead?

hold_final.friendly: I understand. {amount} base per year is where base stays.
hold_final.firm: {amount} base per year is final on base.
hold_final.tight: {amount} base per year is final. Base won't move.

hold_same.friendly: I hear you. Can you tell me more about what's behind that number? Right now I can offer {amount} base per year.
hold_same.firm: I need something new to move on that. The offer is {amount} base per year.
hold_same.tight: Without something new I can't move. The offer is {amount} base per year.

give_lever.friendly: I can add {lever}. Would that help?
give_lever.tight: One thing I can do is {lever}.

lever_unavailable.*: I'm not able to change that right now.

equity.*: Equity is set by level and isn't part of this conversation.

grant_time.*: Of course. Take {time}, and I'll send the terms in writing. The offer on the table is {amount} base per year.

grant_time_noamount.*: Of course. Take {time}, and I'll send the terms in writing.

decline_first.*: Is there anything that would make this work for you?

close_declined.*: Understood. Thank you for your time. I'll leave it there.

close_accepted.*: Wonderful. I'll send the offer letter with {amount} base per year{extras}. Welcome aboard.

answer_other.*: Thanks. To keep us on track, the offer stands at {amount} base per year. What would you like to change?

answer_other_noamount.*: Thanks. What number would work for you?

no_range.*: I can't go into internal budgets, but I can tell you the offer is {amount} base per year.

no_range_noamount.*: I can't go into internal budgets. What number are you looking for?

close_turn_cap.*: I have to wrap up now. The offer is {amount} base per year, and I'd need your answer by the end of the week.
close_turn_cap.none: I have to wrap up now. Please send me your number by the end of the week.

closed_again.*: We've wrapped up. You can end the session now to see your debrief.

restate_offer.*: Sorry about that, we got cut off. Where we left it: {amount} base per year.
restate_offer.none: Sorry about that, we got cut off. What number would work for you?

step_up_grant.friendly: Yes, that's something we can do: {now} now and {later} after {months} months. What would you want to have shown by then?
step_up_grant.firm: We can look at that: {now} now and {later} after {months} months. What would you want to have shown by then?
step_up_grant.tight: That's the one thing I can work with: {now} now and {later} after {months} months. What would you want to have shown by then?

step_up_months_counter.*: Six months, not three. {now} now and {later} after six months. What would you want to have shown by then?

step_up_ask_criteria.*: I can only consider that with clear goals. What would you want to have shown by then?

step_up_not_yet.*: Let's settle base first, then we can talk about later.

step_up_detail.*: Good, that is clear. I'll note those goals.

step_up_writing.*: Yes. I'll put {later} after {months} months{goals} in the offer letter.

step_up_rejected.*: I can't do a later raise on that figure. The offer is {amount} base per year.

pressure.deadline_soft: We'd like to have your answer by the end of next week.
pressure.other_candidates: I should say we are talking to other candidates too.
pressure.deadline_48h: This offer is open for 48 hours.
pressure.standard_role: That figure is standard for the role.

time_text.friendly: until the end of the week

style_brief.friendly: You are Mike, a warm recruiter. You like the candidate and want to close a fair deal.
style_brief.firm: You are Mike, a polite but steady recruiter. You stay friendly and you do not bend easily.
style_brief.tight: You are Mike, a recruiter with a tight budget. You are polite, brief and keen to close fast.
